context:
Goal: the coordinator, triage and lanes can each summarize their context at a size that suits them, without one session changing it for all.
Problem (risk): the built-in command that sets the size writes it into the shared settings file, so one session's choice silently applies to every session on that machine.
Based on (measured): reproduced on Claude Code 2.1.316, Nov 1.
Departs from: main sets one size, 500k, for every session in the shared settings — each kind of session gets its own size.
holds: Step c203 and its draft pull request with the measured figures.

options.gain: Each kind of session gets its own size, and nothing shared changes.
options.how: Each session gets its size from a setting given at launch; no repo change.
options.label: Set the size when a session starts
options.lose: The size is set only at launch; the built-in command to change it mid-session is refused.

options.gain: The built-in command works on each machine.
options.how: The machine's settings file is generated and refreshed, as the cloud does.
options.label: Build the local settings file and refresh it
options.lose: A plain update from the repo no longer refreshes everything on your computer.

options.gain: No stray changes show in git.
options.how: A git filter drops the written value from the repo's view.
options.label: Hide the change from git
options.lose: The size still applies to every session, and the change is hidden from you.

ref: step c203 (a per-session compaction size must not change the shared settings)
reply: Withdrawn: setting the size at launch changes nothing shared and can be undone, so the lane takes a without asking.
title: How should each kind of session get its own compaction size without changing it for every session?
why: It is the only option where one session cannot change another's size, and it needs no change to how your computer updates.
